label: first copy step (input orig(0) right after <DEL>) in short sequences, L=3 or L=4 with first token p/t/3/b/g/r
explanation: Fires almost only at the step right after <DEL> (recall_idx==1, input = first original token fed back, prev_tok = <DEL>); this step holds 98% of activation mass. Strongly gated by sequence length: L=3 (rate 5.5%) and L=4 (1.7%) hold 90% of mass, L=5 holds 8%, L>=6 is near zero. Within short sequences the first token modulates it: p and t give the top activations (max about 0.16), then 3, b, g, r; letters such as o, s, q, k are weak. A small remainder (2% of mass) fires at original-phase t=3 in longer sequences. Silent at the delimiter, at later copy steps, and at t<3. Even inside the predicate, precision is only about 0.4: whether it crosses threshold is a graded mix of L and token identity that no clean boolean captures.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=6: p, t, 3, g; t=5: p, t, 3, b; t=3: k, t, p, r) and the next token to output (most: x, z, c, 1, f, 0; least: k, 2, r, p); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=1, t=3, L=4 & t=5.
